description: HTTP claims checked by hand against the RFC text. Each claim cites the RFC it was read from; inferences name their premises.

nodes.title: Referer is a request header field
nodes.statement: Referer is a request header field: HTTP Semantics defines it among the request context fields, which give information about the context of the request.

nodes.title: Referer is a request header field (RFC 7231)
nodes.statement: RFC 7231 Section 5.5.2 defined the Referer header field under Request Context.

nodes.title: The Referer field name is a misspelling of referrer
nodes.statement: The specification writes the field as "Referer" [sic] and states that it names the "referrer", though the field name is misspelled. The misspelled name is the one defined.

nodes.title: HTTP/1.0 already defined Referer with the same spelling
nodes.statement: HTTP/1.0 (RFC 1945, May 1996) defines "Referer" as a request-header field with the same spelling.

nodes.title: The misspelled name has been kept from HTTP/1.0 to current HTTP
nodes.statement: Because HTTP/1.0 defined the field as "Referer" and current HTTP Semantics still defines it under that name while noting the misspelling, the field has kept the misspelled name from 1996 to today. The specifications do not state a reason for keeping it; any reason given beyond this is not backed by these sources.

nodes.title: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE are the safe methods
nodes.statement: Of the request methods defined by HTTP Semantics, GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE are defined to be safe: their defined semantics are essentially read-only.

nodes.title: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE are the safe methods (RFC 7231)
nodes.statement: RFC 7231 defined GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE as safe.

nodes.title: PUT, DELETE and the safe methods are idempotent
nodes.statement: A method is idempotent if the intended effect of several identical requests is the same as one. Of the methods defined by HTTP Semantics, PUT, DELETE, and the safe methods are idempotent.

nodes.title: PUT, DELETE and the safe methods are idempotent (RFC 7231)
nodes.statement: RFC 7231 defined PUT, DELETE, and safe request methods as idempotent.

nodes.title: Idempotent requests can be retried automatically
nodes.statement: Idempotent requests can be repeated automatically if the connection fails before the client reads the response, because repeating them has the same intended effect.
